display.title: Episode 387: Rabbi Akiva's Negel Vasser and the Drunken Father (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: A Three Weeks show without music: Rabbi Akiva uses his only water in prison to wash his hands, his great rule of Ahavas Yisroel, and the story of Naftali and his drinking father.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during the Three Weeks of 5749, with no music. Uncle Yossi invites children to join Tzivos Hashem, where Torah and mitzvos are the secret weapons that defeat the yetzer hara before Moshiach comes. A brother and sister recite the Shema; she says one of the Twelve Pesukim and he recites a Mishnah from Brachos. The first story: imprisoned for teaching Torah and given no water for three days, Rabbi Akiva uses the precious jug to wash his hands and make a brachah; the amazed ruler frees him and makes him an advisor. Uncle Yossi then explains Rabbi Akiva's teaching that loving your fellow is a great rule of the Torah, since Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem, which is especially needed in the Three Weeks. The second story has no happy ending: Naftali, a fine, respectful boy, leads his drinking father to a drunk in the street, hoping he will see how shameful it is, but the father only asks where to get such a good drink. The lesson, from Parshas Acharei: Hashem shows us other ways of life so that we will not copy them. The show ends with a summer event announcement and the sponsor.
display.lesson: Love every Jew as yourself, cherish every mitzvah, and learn from others' bad ways what not to do.

advisories.note: A father's drinking problem; his son cries about it and fails to change him.
The Naftali story deliberately ends without the father changing.
Rabbi Akiva is jailed and left without water for teaching Torah; he is freed.
